methods.label: Find the sum of the squared dimensions
methods.explanation:
An interior diagonal depends on the sum of the squared dimensions, so we can find its length without determining each dimension separately. Let the positive dimensions of the box be \(x,y,z\) inches. There are four edges of each length, giving
\[
4(x+y+z)=48,
\qquad x+y+z=12.
\]
The six faces form three equal pairs, so the surface-area condition gives
\[
2(xy+xz+yz)=94,
\qquad xy+xz+yz=47.
\]
Expanding the square of the sum now reveals the desired squared lengths:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^2+y^2+z^2
&=(x+y+z)^2-2(xy+xz+yz)\\
&=12^2-2\cdot47=50.
\end{aligned}
\]
A face diagonal has squared length \(x^2+y^2\). Applying the Pythagorean theorem again, using that face diagonal and the perpendicular edge of length \(z\), shows that an interior diagonal has length
\[
\sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2}=\sqrt{50}=5\sqrt2.
\]
Each of the eight vertices has exactly one opposite vertex. Pairing opposite vertices counts each interior diagonal twice, so there are \(8/2=4\) diagonals. Their total length is therefore
\[
4\cdot5\sqrt2=\boxed{20\sqrt2\text{ inches}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
